subject.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser

question: Should OpenClaw enforce a fixed 10 MB maximum for otherwise protocol-valid LSP messages?
rationale: The upstream framing contract defines the byte length but no maximum, so selecting 10 MB intentionally changes compatibility and requires runtime-owner judgment.

options.title: Keep the 10 MB cap
options.body: Accept a conservative fixed memory boundary and document and test that larger valid responses are discarded while stream alignment is preserved.

options.title: Choose another fixed cap
options.body: Select an owner-approved limit based on realistic OpenClaw LSP workloads and cover its exact boundary behavior.

options.title: Fail oversized sessions
options.body: Terminate the session on any over-limit frame instead of draining it, trading recovery for simpler bounded failure semantics.

recommendation.title: Keep the 10 MB cap
recommendation.body: Accept a conservative fixed memory boundary and document and test that larger valid responses are discarded while stream alignment is preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the embedded LSP stdio runtime and has the strongest feature-history connection to its framing behavior.
